text: I've had this cough going on for over three weeks now. It's mostly dry, but sometimes I cough up a little white phlegm, and I've noticed I get quite short of breath when I try to walk or do any physical activity. However, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a critical detail; did the stroke occur before or after the cough began, and are you currently on any anticoagulant medications like warfarin or aspirin? REQUEST TEST: D-dimer level.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal D-dimer result; that makes a pulmonary embolism less likely. Given your history of ischemic stroke and current shortness of breath, have you noticed any swelling in your legs or any chest pain when you take a deep breath?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't have a history of stroke, but to answer your question, I haven't noticed any swelling in my legs. I also don't feel any sharp chest pain when I take a deep breath. I want to emphasize that, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand there is confusion regarding the stroke history; for the purpose of this evaluation, we will proceed based on your current symptoms of a three-week dry cough, white phlegm, and exertional shortness of breath.
